content: The 2024 US National Yo-Yo Contest was held June 21–23 at the Sheraton Downtown in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, organized by the National Yo-Yo League (NYYL) — bringing together the nation's top qualifiers from regional competitions across the United States. title: World YoYo Contest 2020
content: The 2020 World Yo-Yo Contest was originally scheduled to take place in Budapest, Hungary. However, due to the global COVID-19 pandemic, the event was postponed and ultimately canceled entirely. The International Yo-Yo Federation (IYYF) and the local organizing team faced significant financial losses from non-refundable venue deposits and travel arrangements; the IYYF ultimately absorbed these costs to support the Hungarian organizers. Because the entire contest was canceled, no World Yo-Yo Champion titles were awarded for the year 2020.The cancellation of the 2020 event marked an unprecedented pause in the modern competitive yo-yo circuit. To maintain the spirit of global competition during the ongoing lockdowns, the IYYF shifted to a digital format, creating the "Online World Yo-Yo Contest" (OWYYC) which took its place for the 2021 and 2022 seasons. The official, in-person World Yo-Yo Contest did not return until 2023 when it was held in Osaka, Japan.

About the World YoYo Contest 2025

The 2025 World YoYo Contest was held August 7–10 at Centrum Cubex in Prague, Czech Republic — the second time the city hosted the event, following 2014 — drawing over 300 competitors from 43 countries under the organization of IYYF. South Korea's Mir Kim claimed his third consecutive 1A title, becoming only the second player in history to win three or more 1A World Championships after Hiroyuki Suzuki's four-peat (2004–2006, 2012). Japan's Hajime Miura secured his eighth 3A world title — the most in any single division — while Miri Kim took a third consecutive Women's Freestyle crown and Rei Iwakura earned both the Grand Prix and Entertainment Award in Artistic Performance.

title: World YoYo Contest 2026
content:
About the World YoYo Contest 2026

The 2026 World YoYo Contest ran August 13–16 at Arcrea HIMEJI in Himeji, Hyogo, Japan, organized by the IYYF with the Japan Yo-Yo Federation hosting locally. South Korea's Mir Kim won 1A for a fourth straight year (2023–2026), posting a 98.1 — the widest winning margin of the 1A final, nearly five points over runner-up Jakub Doleš (93.1) and third-place Hunter Feuerstein (93.0). Chun Hay Chan (2A), Tomoya Kurita (3A), Koyo Hashimoto (4A), Jihoo Lee (5A), and Yuzuki Takenaga (Women's Freestyle) took the other championship titles, while Masakazu Yamasaki and Yo-Yo Store REWIND TE earned the Artistic and Entertainment Awards in Art & Performance.
